column2: How do I make a widget of shortcuts to anything?
column3: Settings → Widget editor → “＋ New widget” → 🔗 Shortcuts, then “＋ Add shortcuts…”. Three tabs: 🔎 In your database (a person, a place, a Note, an investigation, a search sweep, a Workshop project, a table, a book, a media item, a diagram, a chart, a house, a map, a transcription, a work, a magazine, an employer, a source, a label… with the filters “All (n)”, “👤 People (n)”), 🧭 Screens and tools (screens, your own tabs, lists, tools such as photo retouching or video editing, actions such as “＋ New person” or the backup, tool projects) and 🌐 Website. You can put as many as you like in the same widget, rename them, give them an icon, a colour, show the person’s photo or the media image, add subheadings, arrange them (⠿ or ↑ ↓) and choose tiles, list or small buttons, the size and the number of columns. The widget goes on the dashboard, in your tabs and in a Note; make several if you like.

column2: How do I change my shortcuts directly on the dashboard?
column3: Click the ✎ pencil of the shortcuts widget (on the dashboard, in one of your tabs or in a Note), then “✎ Edit the shortcuts”: “＋ Add shortcuts…” to put in what you want, ⠿ or ↑ ↓ to put them in the order you want, rename them, change their icon, remove them (↶ Undo), choose the layout, then “Save”: the widget redraws straight away. No need to go through Settings.

column2: How do I quickly add a record or a list to my shortcuts?
column3: The ⭐ button (Add to shortcuts), at the far top right of a person’s record, a list, a Note, an investigation or Charts: choose which shortcuts widget to put it in (or create a new one, placed on the dashboard). For a list, the current search, filters and sorting are kept: the shortcut reopens the list just as it was. If the target has been deleted, its tile turns grey “not found” with a “Remove” button (↶ Undo possible).

column2: How do I make a shortcut that creates a new house, a new video edit, a new book…?
column3: Click the ✎ pencil of the shortcuts widget (or Settings → Widget editor) → “＋ Add shortcuts” → “＋ Create…” tab (the same section is also at the top of “🧭 Screens and tools”): one shortcut per editing tool (🏠 New house, 🎬 New video edit, 📐 New book, 🎚️ New photo retouch, ✒️ New drawing, 📰 New announcement, 🎞️ New presentation or slideshow, 📜 New transcription, 🎧 New sound project…). A click on the shortcut opens the tool directly on a new item (an empty document, or the tool’s assistant).

column2: How do I change the order of the search types, or hide some?
column3: Research → “Reorder” (at the bottom of the left column): drag a row or use ↑ ↓, and click the eye to hide or show a type. It is saved straight away (“↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left); “↺ Reset to default” puts back the starting order. A hidden type that another tool opens (a record index, the log…) stays in the menu, marked “(hidden)”.

column2: Is the order of the map backgrounds the same everywhere?
column3: Yes. The order chosen in Settings → Maps and map backgrounds → “Map backgrounds” (categories and backgrounds) is followed by all the background menus: the Map, photo maps, the slideshow, drawn maps, a village’s page (“Map backgrounds as buttons”) and the address plan. An unticked background no longer appears there (unless it is the current one).

column2: How do I create my own tab in the top bar?
column3: Settings → Tab editor → “＋ New tab”. Start from an empty composed page, an app screen, a copy of the dashboard, one of your tabs or a template (My research desk, My village, Tree and map…). In the page, place whatever you want: any app screen (a list, a diagram, a statistic, a person’s record, the map, one of your lists, a Settings tool), with its height and its menus if you like, widgets, your charts, free texts. “↗ Full size” opens the screen. A tab can also be a simple shortcut to a screen. Choose its name and icon; arrange or hide it in Settings → Appearance → “Order of the main menu”, with the other tabs; “Share” turns it into a file.

column2: How do I see who is hidden behind a bar in a statistic?
column3: Click the bar, the column, the slice or the legend line: a window shows the people counted, with a search, sorting by name or by birth and a CSV export. “others” also shows the grouped values.
“others” gathers all the small values: it no longer sets the chart’s scale (otherwise the real values would have almost no colour left). Its stripes say that it goes beyond the scale.

column2: How do I save a chart (or a statistic) as an image?
column3: Charts → My charts → the chart: “PNG image” (sharp, for a forum) or “JPG image” (lighter, for an e-mail), “CSV” for a spreadsheet, “Print / PDF”.

column2: Where do I keep my DNA results?
column3: The “🧬 DNA” tab, hidden at first: Settings → Appearance → menu order, tick “DNA”. Be careful: in France, taking a genealogical DNA test is forbidden outside a medical or research setting (Civil Code art. 16-10, Penal Code art. 226-28-1: a €3,750 fine); the warning and the links to the official texts are in “⚖️ Law and warnings”. The tab stores tests, haplogroups, matches (CSV import), groups (Leeds method), segments (chromosome browser), offers a cM calculator and shows the Y, mt and X lines of the tree. Everything can be set in “⚙️ Settings”.

column2: How do I draw a coat of arms, a logo, or redo an image as vectors?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → “✒️ Vector drawing” (or “🛡️ New coat of arms”), the ✒️ button of a record’s coat of arms, or Settings → Boards → Shapes (✒️ on a shape). Illustrator-style tools: pen, pencil, shapes, text, direct selection of points, layers, groups, masks, Pathfinder, gradients. “Coat of arms” tab: shield, partition, charge, tinctures, charges and automatic blazon. Coat of arms → “Vectorise an image” turns a scanned coat of arms into paths. SVG, PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, BMP import; SVG, PNG, JPG, WEBP, PDF export; save to “My shapes”, to a record’s media or as a coat-of-arms image.

column2: How do I draw the plan of a family house, in 2D and 3D?
column3: Lists → “🏠 Family houses” (or Editing tools → House plan). ⬚ Drag a room: its walls are made automatically and its area is shown; ▬ draws walls by clicking (snapped to the grid, the corners, right angles); 🚪 and 🪟 one click on a wall. Furniture: more than 450 objects (box bed, kneading trough, spinning wheel, stove, longcase clock…), or your own: ⤒ Import an image seen from above, or a 3D file (OBJ with MTL, STL, glTF, GLB). Materials for walls (stone, brick, half-timbering, panelling, wallpaper…) and floors (terracotta tiles, parquet, flagstones…), floors, roof, a scanned plan to trace (scaled in two clicks), and the “3D view” where you turn around and visit. The house is linked to a place, its inhabitants and its censuses, can have several periods (1850, 1900…); each room keeps its memories.

column2: How do I place a chart in a Note, an investigation, the Workshop or a person’s record?
column3: Wherever you place a diagram (📊 block of a Note, “＋ Diagram” of an investigation, of a Workshop project, Diagrams block of a person, dashboard), the window offers: ＋ New diagram, 📊 From a chart (one of yours, an example or an app statistic, drawn with the type of your choice and kept up to date), 📈 One of my charts (a chart from the Chart editor, placed as it is and kept up to date; you choose it in the usual search menu, with its thumbnail, its drawing, where its figures come from and the number of places where it is already placed) and ⤒ Import (a diagram or chart shared as a file, a CSV, a pasted table, a Wikipedia page, an image of a chart). “＋ Create a new chart” leads to the Chart editor.

column2: Where do I create my own chart or diagram?
column3: Everything is done in Settings → Chart editor (formerly called “Statistics editor”): “＋ New chart” (with your own figures or the app’s) and “＋ New diagram” (hemicycle, timeline of a group, organisation chart…). All your charts and diagrams are gathered in Lists → “Charts and diagrams”, as a list or as cards with their thumbnail, where you can search, filter, sort and create others. Charts → “My diagrams” and “My charts” also show them in large. Your charts are stored in your genealogy: they follow the backup and another computer, and can be found in the quick search (⌘K).

column2: How do I sort My diagrams and My charts into folders?
column3: In Charts, left column: “＋ 📁 Folder” to the right of “My diagrams” or “My charts”. A click on a folder opens or closes it (▸ / ▾), and the app remembers; the number on the right says how many items are inside, sub-folders included. On hover: ✎ to rename it, 🗑 to delete it (nothing is lost: what it contains moves up one level). To file a diagram, drag it onto a folder (it lights up in blue) or out of the folders to take it out; drag a folder onto another to make it a sub-folder, or between two folders to change the order (three levels at most). You would rather not drag, or it is one of My charts? Open it and click “📁 File”. After each filing, “↶ Undo” undoes it. The numbers D1, D2… and M1, M2… do not change.

column2: Where are my charts stored, and how do I find one again?
column3: Your charts (made in Settings → Chart editor, formerly “Statistics editor”) are stored in your genealogy, like your records: they follow the full backup, restoration and another computer. Those that were kept in your browser moved there by themselves, once only, without losing anything. To find one: type a few letters of its name in the search menu (“📈 One of my charts”), in the quick search (⌘K or Ctrl+K) or in Lists → “Charts and diagrams”. Each row shows its thumbnail, its drawing (bars, pie…), where its figures come from and in how many places it is placed.

column2: How do I make a chart with my own figures (not those of the tree)?
column3: Settings → Chart editor → “＋ New chart” → “✍️ My own figures” (or, in “2. Chart”, Data → “✍️ My own figures”). A table appears: one row per value (the name, then the figures), “＋ Row”, “＋ Series” for several columns of figures (e.g. 1900 and 1950). You can paste cells from a spreadsheet into a box, “📋 Paste a table” (the first row of headings gives the names of the series), “⤒ Import a CSV”, or “📊 Start from a chart” to copy figures (from one of your charts or an app statistic) and adjust them. With several series, choose a drawing from “My diagrams” (columns, line, stacked, radar…) to see them all.
